$comment: Every duration, cost and curve in the game. Tunable at runtime via the debug panel; never hard-coded in game logic.

garden.$yieldComment: Tending is gone, so there is one multiplier. It keeps the tended figure because the seed economy is balanced against a four-unit harvest; dropping to the untended 1.0 would have cut every harvest by a quarter.
garden.$seedDropComment: Rolled once per unit harvested, not once per plot. Per-plot drains the garden; per-unit is roughly break-even.
garden.$soilComment: Extra units when a crop sits in the soil it wants. A bonus rather than a penalty, so the wrong plot is a missed opportunity and never a punishment.

$freshnessComment: Ageing is a property of the category, not of the individual ingredient. An ingredient is at its stated strength while dewfresh and loses up to a fifth as it dries, so an old batch throws a ratio out. Herbs run the plain schedule, fungus ages twice as fast, and stone and expedition finds never age.
$cauldronComment: Capacity and ingredient count moved to cauldrons.json when the shop stopped having exactly one pot — they are properties of a particular cauldron now, not of the game. What is left here is the rule that applies to every pot alike.

grading.$comment: Purity is 100 at a recipe's exact ratio and 0 at the edge of its cone, and the letter is read straight off it: S from 90. Potency is a separate axis: a small pot on the ratio is an S, a huge one off it is an F.
grading.$sFromComment: Where S starts, by how many essences the potion takes. The simple ones are forgiving; the big mixes ask for nearly the exact ratio. The bands below are written for S at 90, and every band but F moves up by the same amount as S does.

economy.$startingComment: Seeds and spores come from merchants and expeditions, so a new shop starts with one clean herb of each essence and one cave species - enough to make the five potions it already knows.
